alignments.note: Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied *The* that makes it one (rule 46), headed on the lexeme.

One English word carries the negation, the time and the preposition's adverbial relation alike, so the three morphemes share one unit across the verb they negate (rules 30, 35, 40); no English word is spent on לְ or on עוֹלָם apart from the others. The corpus heads *never* both ways; I head on the negative, which is what distinguishes it from a bare *ever*, and the temporal noun is the competing head.
Auxiliaries join the verb; head on the lexical verb (rule 24). Unit discontinuous around *never* under rule 25.
Waw rendered by the connective *But* the ASV wrote for it (rule 14).
Substantival adjective with the supplied *the* that makes it one (rule 46).

Corrected: the auxiliary joins the finite verb, but the supplied *in* does not. שָׁכַן is intransitive and אָרֶץ is an accusative of place rather than a bare direct object, so rule 44's valency sentence does not reach it.

Corrected: *in* is the function word the ASV supplies for an adverbial accusative of place and belongs to the noun whose case-function licenses it (rule 33, as *to your mountain*); the ASV writes *dwell upon* elsewhere, so another relation would have served and rule 33's own test sends the word to the noun rather than to the predicate. The supplied *the* joins the same noun under rule 15. The competing reading gives *in* to the verb under rule 44.

review_notes: Corrected: *in* before *the land* moved from the verb's unit to אָרֶץ's. Rule 44's supplied-preposition sentence is conditioned on a bare direct object, and אָרֶץ after intransitive שָׁכַן is an accusative of place; rule 33's closing test — whether the English predicate admits another word before the complement — sends *in* to the noun, since the ASV writes *dwell upon* as well as *dwell in*.

The flagged three-morpheme unit לְ + עוֹלָם + בַּל → *never* is genuinely indivisible: no English word is spent on any one of the three, so rule 30's condition is met and rule 2 has no allocation to test. Head taken on the negative, with the temporal noun named as the competing head (rule 35).
The marginal *Or, earth* was read and set aside; the printed *land* governs.
